maria: FYI rolled heuristic tuning PR (#4827) to canary at 09:12. Changed token_budget_target from 1024 -> 512 for short-context routes to favor lower latency batching.
aj: saw p95 jump on small requests within 5m of deploy. Dashboard: p50 ~ stable, p95 from ~120ms -> ~340ms. Throughput down ~18%.
kevin: that's surprising; lowering token_budget should make quicker batches and lower latency. Do you have traces?
sasha: deploy-bot: canary rollout completed to 10% on hosts prod-eu-*. No automatic rollback. :bot:
deploy-bot: rollout:canary completed 2026-03-05T09:15:22Z
maria: attaching quick profiler snapshot (repro with loadtest):
```
# pprof summary
cpu: 90s
samples: 9000
40.0% runtime/lock
22.0% serving/dispatcher.Dispatch
15.0% runtime.MSpan
10.0% kernel/kvcache.Lookup
```
```
flame: lots of time in dispatcher queuing and lock contention, worker threads idle waiting for batch completion.
```
aj: sounds like we're forming batches too eagerly and then waiting on the slowest request in batch (head-of-line blocking). Lower token_budget made batch sizes smaller but increased batch frequency -> more contention and kernel selection overhead.
luis: I pulled logs: batch_size median dropped from 8 -> 3 on the short routes. But batch formation rate doubled, kernel switching calls up by 2.7x. Kernel selection path is not free.
kevin: can we correlate with KV cache hit rate? If we reduce batch size we may lose prefix reuse between tokens in same request (or between requests) leading to more KV misses and recompute.
sasha: kvcache stats show increased evictions: evict/sec +45% on those canary nodes. Miss rate +9%. That would increase per-token kernel work.
maria: reproduction steps I used:
1) run k6 script short_ctx.json @ 200rps hitting /generate?max_tokens=40
2) observe p95 after 2m
3) run pprof capture from /debug/pprof/profile

Command: `k6 run short_ctx.js --vus 50 --duration 3m`
aj: I have a quick hypothesis: the dispatcher wait-time heuristic uses token_budget_target but also a min_wait_ms gating. PR reduced token target but didn't change min_wait_ms, so we ended up with many partial batches still waiting the same min_wait_ms -> more kernel churn.
kevin: also check kernel selection cache: when batch sizes vary a lot we might call selectKernel() per-batch instead of per-worker-affinity. Cost adds up.
oncall: paging @maria @aj oncall: looking into hotspot nodes now.
luis: I ran microbenchmark on canary host: single-request latency (no batching) same as baseline. Batching latency increases are from batch formation + kernel overhead.
sasha: logs show `select_kernel` calls jump and `kvcache.lookup` increases latency tail. Example lines: `INFO select_kernel model=gptx batch_size=3 latency=1.4ms` repeated a lot.
maria: decision proposal: rollback canary to previous heuristic while we fix: revert token_budget_target and add automated test to simulate short-context workloads. Also instrument a per-batch metric for kernel_selection_time and dispatcher_lock_wait_ms.
aj: agree rollback now. I'll trigger and create follow-up ticket with profiling checklist.
kevin: follow-ups:
- add unit/integration test for batch-size distribution with different token_budget and min_wait_ms combos
- memoize kernel selection per worker for short windows (e.g., 50ms)
- tune KV cache admission to avoid churn for short-lived prefixes
- add histogram for per-batch select_kernel time
sasha: I'll post pprof + raw logs to the ticket.
deploy-bot: rollback:canary invoked by @aj at 09:32:11Z. Rollback completed 09:34:00Z.
aj: post-rollback metric quick check: p95 back to ~130ms within 3m, throughput recovered. I'll keep the canary disabled until we implement the fixes.
maria: thanks all. I'll own the ticket for heuristic rework and the test harness. Putting notes in #perf-reviews and linking tickets. :thumbsup:
kevin: nits: let's add a regression test in CI that fails if p95 increases >40% on synthetic short-route profile when we change batching heuristics.
maria: noted.
